mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay depressed while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, discretionary trip chaining stays weak and retail visits stay below the prior four-week mean over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES staying below -20 and RESIDENTIAL staying above +3 for most weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rebound in PARKS from a negative or near-zero week signals substitution toward outdoor leisure, which diverts discretionary time and spending away from retail-and-recreation for the following one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points week-on-week from a subzero week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall or stay below its recent mean within 1-2 weeks after a PARKS jump of 10 points or more from a subzero level.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT recovers faster than WORKPLACES, the same mobility shock is likely caused by fewer access constraints rather than more office demand, and retail traffic then rises over the next four weeks through easier cross-purpose travel.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases while WORKPLACES stays below -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week mean even though TRANSIT improves by at least 5 points while WORKPLACES remains deeply negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM indicates more frequent essential errands and neighborhood circulation, which spills over into nearby retail purchases and lifts RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 2 weeks after GROCERY_PHARM rises for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both rise together, households are reallocating time to local recreation and home-based activity, which suppresses retail outings and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS above +10 and RESIDENTIAL above +4 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 28 days after a week in which PARKS exceeds +10 and RESIDENTIAL exceeds +4.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES improves without a matching rise in TRANSIT, the return to office is partial and mostly local, so retail recovery is muted; only a joint improvement in commuting and work mobility would lift RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 4 points while TRANSIT stays below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises within 2 weeks even though WORKPLACES improves and TRANSIT remains deeply negative.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility means households are spending less time at home and more time out of the dwelling, which should translate into slightly higher discretionary retail visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 1.5 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior four-week mean after RESIDENTIAL drops for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous upswing in GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT indicates active multi-stop travel and restored network circulation, a pattern that should spill into broader retail-and-recreation demand within one to two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines within 1-2 weeks despite both GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT moving upward together.
